recorded.outcome:q-callable-as-supplier: Section 'A Lambda Is an Object of Whatever Interface Its Context Expects': getInterfaces() output shows the Callable lambda implements only [interface java.util.concurrent.Callable], `c instanceof Supplier` prints false, and the text says: 'The `Callable` is not a `Supplier`, although its body is the same. A cast, `(Supplier<String>) c`, compiles, since one interface type may be cast to another, and throws `ClassCastException` when it runs.' The quiz uses Long where the page uses String, but the page's example matches the quiz case.

recorded.outcome:q-billing-class-files: Section 'The Compiler Turns a Lambda Into a Private Method and an invokedynamic Call': `ls *.class` shows only Jobs$1.class and Jobs.class; `javap -p Jobs` lists the constructor, main and `private static void lambda$main$0()`; the text says 'The anonymous class is `Jobs$1.class`, created with `new`; the lambda has no file. Its body became `lambda$main$0`, a private method of `Jobs`'. The Reference table row 'Class file from javac' says the same: lambda 'none; body in a private `lambda$<method>$<n>` method', anonymous class '`Outer$1.class`'.

recorded.outcome:q-lambda-cache-key: Section 'A Lambda's Identity Is Not Promised: Keep the Instance You Need to Find Again': 'On HotSpot, a lambda that captures nothing comes back from the same site as the same object every time, and one that captures anything is allocated fresh' (output 'capturing, same value: false'); 'Lambdas don't override `equals`, so `equals` is `==`, and two lambdas with the same text, or the same lambda evaluated twice with the same captured value, are not equal'; and 'a lambda is no use as a map key (found only with the instance that was put in)'. The lambda captures the parameter `region`, which matches the page's own capturing example `of(String region)`.

recorded.pass:q-lambda-cache-key:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-lambda-cache-key:b: Refuted, though only implicitly. The page states the allocation rule purely by capture ('a lambda that captures nothing comes back from the same site as the same object every time'), and the opening problem has a lambda passed as an argument, `feed.subscribe(q -> onPrice(q))`, about which it says 'Even one shared site wouldn't help, because `q -> onPrice(q)` captures `this` and is new each time', which blames capture, not argument position. Partly true: the count (1,000) is correct; only the reason is wrong.
